topSources: The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s111

rows.answer:
Under Section 7 of the Odisha House Rent Control Act, 1967 (Odisha), a landlord who seeks to evict a tenant for non-payment of rent shall apply to the Controller for a direction in that behalf [4].

Conditions and time limits:
- The tenant has not paid or tendered the rent due in respect of the house within thirty days after the expiry of the time fixed in the agreement of tenancy, or in the absence of any such agreement, by the last day of the month next following that for which the rent is payable [4].
- When an application is made for eviction on the ground of default in payment of rent, the tenant shall remit the arrear rent as admitted by up to the date of remittance to the landlord or deposit the same with the Controller, failing which the tenant shall not be entitled to contest the proceedings [4].
- If the Controller is satisfied that the tenant's default was not wilful, the Controller may give the tenant a reasonable time not exceeding fifteen days to pay or tender the rent due up to the date of such payment, and upon such payment or tender, the application shall be rejected [4].

rows.answer:
- Compensation for a hit and run motor accident where the identity of the vehicle cannot be ascertained despite reasonable efforts can be claimed in accordance with Section 161 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [1].
- An application for compensation can be made by the person who has sustained injury, by the owner of the property, by all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased where death has resulted, or by any duly authorized agent, under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [2].
- Where all the legal representatives have not joined, the application shall be made on behalf of or for the benefit of all of them, and those who have not joined shall be impleaded as respondents, pursuant to Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [2].
- The application may be made, at the claimant's option, either to the Claims Tribunal having jurisdiction over the area where the accident occurred, or to the Claims Tribunal within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the claimant resides or carries on business or the defendant resides, as provided in Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [2].

rows.question: Can I file for divorce in the first year of marriage?

As a general rule under Indian law, no petition for divorce can be presented to a court within one year of the date of the marriage [1][3]. This restriction applies under Section 14 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, and Section 29 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954 [1][3]. Similarly, under Section 32B of the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936, no suit for divorce by mutual consent shall be filed unless one year has lapsed since the date of the marriage [6]. 

Conditions and time limits:
- A court or district court may allow an application to present a divorce petition before one year has elapsed only on the ground of exceptional hardship to the petitioner or exceptional depravity on the respondent [1][3].
- When considering such an application, the court must have regard to the interests of any children of the marriage and whether there is a reasonable probability of reconciliation between the parties before the expiration of the one-year period [1][3].

The period of limitation in the case of any dispute which is required to be referred to arbitration shall be regulated by the provisions of the Limitation Act, 1963 as if the dispute was a suit and the arbitrator is a civil court, according to Section 43 of the Special Economic Zones Act, 2005 [5].
